html:
The Xiongnu were a confederation of nomadic peoples who ruled the eastern Eurasian steppe, centred on Mongolia, from 209 BCE to the late 1st century CE. They were the first great steppe empire, and the main rival of Han China.

Modu Chanyu founded the empire in 209 BCE. He drove the Yuezhi out of the Gansu corridor and in 200 BCE trapped the first Han emperor at Baideng. The Han then bought peace through the heqin system: princesses for marriage and yearly gifts of silk, grain and wine.

Under Emperor Wu the Han changed course. From 133 BCE they fought long, costly wars to push the Xiongnu north and take the western corridor. Emperor Wu sent Zhang Qian west to look for allies against them, a mission that helped open the Silk Road. The walls begun by the Qin were extended in these years.

Key turns:

  • 209 BCE: Modu takes power and unites the tribes.
  • 200 BCE: Han defeat at Baideng.
  • 133 BCE onward: Han offensives.
  • 48 CE: split into a southern group that submitted to the Han and a northern group that stayed free.
  • 89 to 91 CE: Han and southern armies broke the northern Xiongnu.

The Xianbei took over the Mongolian steppe. Southern Xiongnu settled inside China and later founded short-lived states in the north. Whether they had any link to the Huns who reached Europe in the 4th century is unproven.
sum: The Xiongnu were a confederation of nomadic peoples who ruled the eastern Eurasian steppe, centred on Mongolia, from 209 BCE to the late 1st century CE. They were the first great steppe empire, and the main rival of Han China.
